summary_paragraph: The patient, a paraplegic woman with a history of recurrent pneumonias and UTIs, was admitted for hypoxia and productive cough. She was found to have Klebsiella pneumonia and sepsis, requiring intubation and pressor support. After initial improvement, she was extubated but developed right lung collapse and pleuritic pain. She later requested re-intubation due to worsening dyspnea, during which she suffered a PEA arrest likely due to airway plugging. She was resuscitated, underwent bronchoscopy, and was stabilized. A tracheostomy was placed, and she gradually improved with minimal ventilator support. Her anemia remained stable, and she was discharged to extended care on trach mask with a Dobhoff tube, awake and alert.
